originality.rationale: The all-real-cap minimum enclosing Euclidean sphere and complete vertex-contact phase classification are not supplied by the two inspected recent primary manuscripts or the two closest same-object published results. The published matroid theorem applies to Boolean vertices for integral caps; its projection argument fails for fractional vertices and gives the wrong center at n=5, tau=8/5. The published capped-cube John theorem is about the maximally inscribed ellipsoid, which does not determine minimum enclosing radius or outer contacts. Targeted multi-alias searches found no covering all-real-cap theorem, but worldwide priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The uniform one-halfspace cut is a natural, currently researched hypercube/knapsack polytope; its outer metric geometry is not determined by volume approximations, graph diameter or the same-body John ellipsoid. The claim settles center, squared radius and all contacts uniformly for an infinite real-parameter family and identifies two sharp thresholds, a strict radius plateau despite polytope growth, and a Boolean-to-fractional contact exchange. An integer-rank projection theorem fails at fractional caps, giving a substantive and motivated boundary phenomenon beyond a single computation.
